# Python asyncio mastery — event loop, tasks, streams and concurrency patterns

Curated by Skill Harbor — @bobmatnyc's asyncio skill: a genuinely deep guide to async Python, from the first event-loop diagram to production patterns. Covers coroutines and awaitables, tasks and TaskGroups, the event loop (run, run_until_complete, call_soon), concurrency vs parallelism (threads vs processes vs async), synchronization primitives (Lock, Event, Semaphore, Condition, Barrier), queues and producer/consumer pipelines, async iterators and generators, streams (StreamReader/StreamWriter), async context managers, timeouts, cancellation, shielding, error handling and retries, real-world patterns (gathering results, connection pools, rate limiting, fan-out/fan-in, background tasks), plus an asyncio vs Trio vs Curio comparison and learning resources. Honest caveats: knowledge base stated for Python 3.8+ — verify newer syntax against your interpreter; this is a reference guide, not a code fixer — the agent explains and writes async code with you. MIT licensed (manifest record authoritative). Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
